title: bmus comms message
description: One NDJSON line on the bridge<->combadge comms channel (spec/initial-plan-2026-10-16.md §6, D3). Every message shares this envelope; `type` selects the body shape via the if/then rules in `allOf`. Beam->bridge types: hello, heartbeat, progress, usage, finding, hail, checkpoint_ready, report, error, consult_reply. Bridge->beam types: ack, order, answer, consult, checkpoint, stand_down, recall, belay, correction. consult and consult_reply are Command-lane only (Phase 3) and are defined here for forward compatibility; nothing emits or handles them in Phase 1. Envelope and bodies reject unknown properties so drift between the Go bridge and the TypeScript combadge is caught by the golden tests; the only free-form object is a hail's `context`.

v.description: Protocol version. Bumped only on incompatible changes.

seq.description: Per-direction sequence; the two directions are independent. Beam->bridge: the combadge outbox seq. It starts at 1 and is monotonic for the life of the combadge's outbox file, not per process: a restarted combadge resumes from the outbox. The bridge dedups on (crew, seq) in the inbox table and acks; 0 is rejected for beam->bridge types so `ack` seq 0 can mean nothing recorded yet. Bridge->beam: the command id the combadge dedups on (D3), except for `ack`, which is idempotent and not deduped.

crew.description: Crew member id the message is from (beam->bridge) or to (bridge->beam).

order.description: Order id the message belongs to. Required and non-empty for order-bound types (progress, usage, finding, hail, checkpoint_ready, report, order, answer, checkpoint, recall, belay, correction); optional for hello, heartbeat, ack, error, stand_down, consult and consult_reply, which may be about the beam or tour rather than one order. Either absent or non-empty.

type.description: Message type; selects the body shape.

ts.description: Time the sender created the message, RFC 3339.

is_beam_to_bridge.description: Matches beam->bridge types, whose seq (the outbox seq) starts at 1.

order_bound.description: Envelope constraint for messages that belong to one order: `order` must be present (the envelope's minLength makes it non-empty). `order` is redeclared here because ajv strict mode (strictRequired) wants required properties defined alongside.

hello.description: beam->bridge. Sent by the combadge at the start of each attach session.

protocol.description: Highest protocol version the combadge speaks.

harness.description: Harness driving the agent, e.g. sdk or holodeck.

model.description: The harness's default model, the one an order without `model` runs on. Absent when the harness doesn't know it.

heartbeat.description: beam->bridge. Periodic beam health (every 10s in Phase 1); missing beats trigger the sickbay probe.

outbox_depth.description: Outbox entries not yet acked by the bridge.

progress.description: beam->bridge. Agent-reported progress; goes straight to the captain's log, not into workflows.

usage_report.description: beam->bridge. Running usage of the order on this beam (#117), cumulative over every run and query of the order on this beam, combadge restarts included; input counts cache reads and writes. Counts never decrease. Sent every 10 turns and at every checkpoint, stop and report. The latest report for (order, beam) is the one with the highest envelope seq, which is monotonic across combadge restarts.

turns.description: Main-loop turns; a subagent's are not counted.

finding.description: beam->bridge. Something a crew member found while working that deserves its own tracker issue (#153). The bridge keeps it on the order and files it as an issue when the order's mission ends. A finding with a key already recorded on the order replaces it; an order keeps at most 20 keys. Goes straight to the store, never into a workflow. title's and body's limits are in characters here; the bridge and combadge count body in bytes of UTF-8.

key.description: The finding's key within its order, which fits a tracker marker key. Reusing it replaces the earlier finding.

title.description: The issue's title: one line, without control characters.

body.description: The issue's body (markdown). At most 32 KiB of UTF-8.

labels.description: Labels for the issue, beside the bridge's own: no commas, control characters or surrounding spaces, and none starting with bmus: in any letter case, which the bridge reserves.

blocked_by.description: What the finding waits on: the key of another finding of the same order, or a tracker ref (#12 or owner/name#12).

finding_ref.description: A tracker ref a finding may be blocked by: #<number>, or <owner>/<name>#<number>. The bridge makes it canonical when it files the finding, and drops one its tracker refuses.

hail.description: beam->bridge. A question or permission request the agent is blocked on. Deliberate deviation from the spec §6 example: the bridge generates hail ids (H-0001, store.InsertHail), so this body carries no hail_id. It carries `ref`, the combadge's own id for the hail (unique per combadge process), which the bridge echoes in the `answer`. Conventions: a tool_approval hail carries options ["allow", "deny"]; a clarifying_question hail carries one question, with or without options.

ref.description: Combadge-local hail id, echoed back in the answer.

category.description: Hail category: clarifying_question, tool_approval, order_split (Command splitting its order into child orders, #155), order_reorder (Command changing the base and after of orders nobody has started, #148), tracker_comment or tracker_close (a request to comment on or close a tracker item, #54), budget (the harness is over its order's budget, #119); open so later categories (scope_change, destructive, egress, ...) fit.

options.description: Choices offered to the decider; absent or empty means free-text answer.

context.description: Free-form context (files, diff stat, tool input...). The only open object in the protocol, except for an order_split hail's (order_split_context), an order_reorder hail's (order_reorder_context), a tracker request's (tracker_comment_context, tracker_close_context) and a budget hail's (budget_context).

budget_context.description: A budget hail's context (#119): the order's usage and limit in tokens (input, cache reads and writes, and output) and in main-loop turns. Used counts the usage recorded on the order's other beams plus the harness's own; a zero limit is unlimited. The bridge writes the hail's question from it.

tracker_comment_context.description: A tracker_comment hail's context (#54): the item to comment on and the comment. The bridge checks it again and runs an allowed request with its own credentials.

tracker_close_context.description: A tracker_close hail's context (#54): the item to close and why. The bridge checks it again and runs an allowed request with its own credentials.

order_split_context.description: An order_split hail's context: the child orders Command asks to split its order into. The bridge checks it again (bridge.checkSplit). An allowed split is answered with option 0 and the new orders' ids, comma separated, as the decision.

priority.description: 0 routine, 1 yellow, 2 red. Absent: the parent order's.

after.description: Earlier children of the same split, by 0-based index, this child waits on until each is done (#142). The bridge refuses its own or a later index.

order_reorder_context.description: An order_reorder hail's context (#148): the changes Command asks for to the base and after of orders nobody has started, and why. The bridge checks it again (bridge.checkReorder) and writes the question from the orders' current and proposed bases and afters. An allowed one is applied change by change, each rechecked; the answer has option 0 and what applied and what was skipped as the decision, or option 1 when nothing applied.

items.$comment: minProperties: order and at least one of onto, after_add and after_remove.

onto.description: The order's new base_ref: order:<id> or a ref. At most 256 bytes of UTF-8: the bridge and combadge count bytes, and maxLength, which counts characters, is only the schema's looser bound.

after_add.description: Orders to add to its after.

after_remove.description: Orders to drop from its after; not one its base implies.

order_id.description: An order id as the bridge makes them.

checkpoint_ready.description: beam->bridge. A checkpoint is on the beam's disk for the bridge to scp into the cargo bay. Paths are absolute on the beam.

repos.description: One bundle per repo of the order, in the order's list order.

handover_path.description: Handover note written by the agent.

stopping.description: True on the checkpoint that answers a stand_down or recall: the harness stops after it and the order ends with no report or error. Absent means the order runs on.

held.description: The refs of the hails a park checkpoint holds (#145): the run parked on them, and the bridge keeps them open if the order parks before they are answered. Absent on any other checkpoint.

report.description: beam->bridge. Final result of the order. The bridge pulls every repo's bundle into the cargo bay, fetches it into its clone as `bmus/<order>`, then marks the order done.

repos.description: One bundle per repo of the order, in the order's list order.

artifacts.description: Paths or references to produced artifacts.

work_repo.description: The work in one repo of an order, as a git bundle on the beam's disk.

bundle_path.description: Absolute path on the beam of a git bundle of `branch` minus the order's base commit, or of its whole history when the branch has no commits past it (git refuses an empty bundle).

commit.description: The commit `branch` points at in the bundle.

full_bundle_path.description: A checkpoint's full bundle (#145), when bundle_path holds only what came after the previous checkpoint's commit: the bridge takes it when the incremental one doesn't verify. Absent when bundle_path is the full one.

wip_bundle_path.description: A checkpoint's WIP bundle (#145): refs/bmus/wip/<order> and refs/bmus/kept-wip/<order>, those that exist, minus `branch` at `commit`. A file of its own, so the commits land even when the WIP can't. Absent when there is no WIP.

repo_name.description: A repo name in the bridge's registry, and a directory name on the bridge and the beam. `in`, `out` and all-digit names are reserved: `<work-dir>/<order>/in/` holds the bundles going in, `out/` the bundles coming back and numbered dirs the checkpoints.

error.description: beam->bridge. Harness crash, tool failure, budget exceeded. With an order set it fails that order.

code.description: Optional machine-readable code, e.g. budget_exceeded or exit_137.

consult_reply.description: beam->bridge, Command lane only (Phase 3; unused in Phase 1). Command's structured decision on a consulted hail (spec D7). Regulations re-check it and low confidence escalates.

hail_id.description: Bridge hail id from the consult.

option.description: Index into the hail's options when answering with one.

answer.description: Free-text answer when the hail has no options.

ack.description: bridge->beam. Lets the combadge trim its outbox. Idempotent: the combadge applies every ack and does not dedup acks by command id.

seq.description: Highest contiguous beam->bridge seq the bridge has recorded; 0 means none yet.

order.description: bridge->beam. Assigns the mission named by the envelope's `order`.

repos.description: Repos the order works on, each shipped onto the beam as a git bundle before the order (D6). The combadge clones each into `<work-dir>/<order>/<name>` and checks out `bmus/<order>` before the harness starts. A list from the start; a Phase 1 bridge sends exactly one.

budget_tokens.description: The order's current token limit: its resolved budget times 1 + budget_extended. 0 means no budget.

budget_turns.description: The order's current limit of main-loop turns, as budget_tokens. Absent or 0 means no budget.

used_tokens.description: Tokens the bridge recorded for the order on its other beams. The harness is over budget when this plus its own count for the order passes budget_tokens. Absent means 0.

used_turns.description: Main-loop turns the bridge recorded for the order on its other beams, as used_tokens. Absent means 0.

model.description: Model to run the order on: the order's own, else the crew member's, else its division's default. Opaque to the bridge; the harness checks it when the order starts and fails the order if it is unknown. Absent means the harness's default.

handover.description: Handover note of the checkpoint the order resumes from; each repo's bundle then carries that checkpoint's commits. Absent on a fresh order.

grants.description: Tool calls the captain allowed on a hail carried across a park (#145), which the order's earlier run never got to make: the harness lets the same call through once, without a hail. Absent when there are none.

name.description: Repo name in the bridge's registry, and the checkout's directory name.

base_ref.description: Git ref the work starts from, as the captain gave it.

bundle_path.description: Absolute path on the beam of a git bundle holding branch `bmus/<order>` at base_ref's commit, with its full history.

answer.description: bridge->beam. Decision on a hail. Echoes the hail's `ref` so the combadge can resume the waiting callback, and adds the bridge-generated `hail_id`. For a tool_approval hail, `option` 0 ("allow") allows the tool; any other option, or none, denies it with `decision` as the deny message. For a clarifying_question hail, `decision` is the answer text and `option` is set when a listed option was picked.

decision.description: The answer text (the chosen option's text when one was picked).

option.description: Index into the hail's options, when one was picked.

budget.description: The order's new limit, on a budget hail's answer that extends it (#119): tokens and main-loop turns, 0 for unlimited. A harness given an extend without it (from an older bridge) keeps its old limit.

consult.description: bridge->beam, Command lane only (Phase 3; unused in Phase 1). A hail plus the context Command cannot see on its own (spec D7).

crew.description: Crew member who hailed. Absent for a hail a bridge workflow raised, which has no crew member or order (#152).

order.description: Order the hail belongs to (not Command's own). Absent for a hail a bridge workflow raised (#152).

context.description: The hail's free-form context, passed through.

recent_log.description: Recent captain's-log lines for the order.

model.description: Model Command answers on: its crew member's, else its division's default. Opaque to the bridge. Absent means the harness's default.

checkpoint.description: bridge->beam. Reach a safe point and checkpoint; answered by checkpoint_ready.

stand_down.description: bridge->beam. End the tour on this beam (watch change); checkpoint first if an order is in progress.

recall.description: bridge->beam. Checkpoint and give the order back to the pool.

belay.description: bridge->beam. Abandon the order without checkpointing.

correction.description: bridge->beam. The captain countermanded a decision made without them (Command's, or a captain timeout's default_option) after the agent already had the first answer (phase 3 plan section 6). Not a second answer: a running session is told of it; with no run for the order it is logged and dropped.

hail_id.description: Bridge hail id (H-0001, ...) of the countermanded decision.

ref.description: The order the hail belongs to, as the envelope's order.

note.description: The new decision and the captain's reason.

question.description: The hail's question, so a run that never got the first answer (one resumed after a park) can name what was overridden. Optional.
